description_full: PT Medco Energi Internasional Tbk, together with its subsidiaries, explores for and produces oil and gas in Indonesia, Asia, Africa, the Middle East, and the United Kingdom. It operates through Exploration and Production of Oil and Gas; Services; Power; Chemicals; and Trading segments. The company operates an independent power producer in the gas, geothermal, and other renewables sectors, as well as manages a portfolio of onshore and offshore assets in the Middle East, Africa, and the Asia Pacific. It is also involved in copper and gold mining operations in Sumbawa and Nusa Tenggara; and providing operation and maintenance services, and support services for oil and gas activities. The company was formerly known as PT Medco Energi Corporation and changed its name to PT Medco Energi Internasional Tbk in 2000. The company was founded in 1980 and is headquartered in Jakarta, Indonesia. PT Medco Energi Internasional Tbk operates as a subsidiary of Pt Medco Daya Abadi Lestari.

financial_summary: PT Medco Energi Internasional Tbk is a small-cap energy business with a $1.7B market cap on $2.4B of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +1% over the past three years, which puts it in mature, slow-growth territory. Operating margins are contracting by -4.6pp, the first warning that competitive pressure is eroding the franchise.
Returns on capital run at 9% against a 8% cost of capital, which means the business barely earns its keep economically, with gross margins sitting at 43%.
The business throws off $391M in free cash flow — roughly 16 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders.
On the balance sheet, debt is heavy at 4.7× net debt/EBITDA, and leverage like that is what turns a bad year into a permanent loss, and thin 2.1× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Management returns a meaningful 6.3% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and within its sector the business captures 2.7× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
